claims.claim: The web app renders a static foundation landing shell with semantic landmarks, a skip link, and explicit status disclosures.
A shared token package defines the initial ocean, sky, white, sand, and seafoam palette.
The API exposes a fixed, non-leaking liveness response.
The API checks real database connectivity and truthfully reports HTTP 200/ready when reachable or HTTP 503/not-ready when it is not.
Every API error response uses a typed envelope with a stable error code and a request ID, and every response carries a matching X-Request-ID header.
Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, never logged or returned, and login issues an expiring, revocable session token that is rejected once expired or revoked.

Server-side role checks and organization-scoped queries prevent a member of one organization from reading or acting on another organization's data, returning a not-found response instead of leaking existence.
Login and the admin-only demonstration endpoint each append an immutable audit event; audit rows reject in-place updates and deletes at the database level.
The seed script creates the same synthetic organizations, memberships, and demo accounts every time it runs against an empty database, with no real personal data.
A typed TypeScript client package covers every implemented API endpoint (health, login, /me, org members) with response types mirrored from the API schemas.

The web app renders Home, Initiatives, Projects, Evidence, and About Justin pages behind one accessible shared shell with a skip link and current-page navigation, and reuses shared status and case-study card primitives.

The web app renders a static Zion Labs archive from a checked-in Batcomputer Portfolio snapshot with four featured flagships and nineteen grouped secondary labs, without runtime GitHub access or copied assets.
